seo.shortDescription: Searchable 2026 U.S. tariff table for all 402 HTS Chapter 87 lines — cars, SUVs, EVs, pickups, heavy trucks, buses, auto parts, motorcycles, e-bikes, bicycles and trailers. Base rates Free to 25%, the 25% Section 232 auto, parts and truck duties, the 15% EU, Japan and Korea deal rates, USMCA rules and the extra duty by country.

overview.intro:
Chapter 87 covers road vehicles and their parts: tractors, buses, cars and SUVs, trucks, special-purpose vehicles, chassis and bodies, auto parts, motorcycles and e-bikes, bicycles, wheelchairs, strollers and trailers — 402 tariff lines. Base rates are low (Free to 25%: cars 2.5%, auto parts 2.5% or Free, pickups and most trucks 25%), but since 2025 almost every vehicle and most parts also pay a **Section 232** duty: 25% on passenger vehicles and light trucks (from April 3, 2025), 25% on listed auto parts (from May 3, 2025), 25% on medium- and heavy-duty trucks and 10% on buses (from November 1, 2025).

Trade deals cap cars and listed parts at **15% in total** for the EU, Japan and South Korea (and parts from Taiwan), and UK cars pay **10%** inside a 100,000-vehicle annual quota. **USMCA** cars and trucks from Mexico and Canada pay the 25% only on the value of their non-U.S. content once Commerce approves it; USMCA parts pay nothing. Chinese electric vehicles pay **127.5%**. Goods outside the Section 232 actions — motorcycles, bicycles, e-bikes, wheelchairs, strollers, trailers and parts that are not vehicle parts — pay the 2026 Section 301 duty for their country instead.

In 2025 the United States imported **$337.9B** of Chapter 87 goods, led by Mexico ($124.2B), Japan ($46.2B), Canada ($45.8B), South Korea ($38.3B), Germany ($27.8B). Cars (8703) were $183.8B and auto parts (8708) $84.7B. Search the table by product or code: each row shows the base rate and the extra duties that can apply.

stats.note: Section 232 cars and light trucks: 74; auto parts: 119 (when they are car or light-truck parts); trucks: 58; buses: 10; truck and bus parts: 99; metals: 88. 2026 Section 301 and Brazil: all 402 (lifted for Section 232 goods). China lists: 367; China 100% EV duty: 29. Canada Section 338: 7 (also on USMCA goods).

productGroups.label: Tractors: road tractors for semi-trailers, farm and track-laying tractors
productGroups.blurb: Farm and track-laying tractors are Free at base; road tractors for semi-trailers (8701.21–8701.29) pay 4%. Road tractors also pay the 25% Section 232 truck duty; other tractors carry the Section 232 metals duty on equipment (15% in total for farm tractors, 25% for single-axle, track-laying and other non-farm tractors, 15% from the deal partners).

productGroups.label: Buses, coaches and vans for 10 or more people
productGroups.blurb: Buses, coaches and 10+ passenger vans pay 2%, plus the 10% Section 232 bus duty from every country, USMCA included. Electric buses (8702.40, 8702.90) from China add 100% (note 31).

productGroups.label: Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs, hybrids, ATVs, golf carts and snowmobiles
productGroups.blurb: Cars, SUVs, minivans, EVs and hybrids pay 2.5% at base, plus the 25% Section 232 automobile duty: 15% in total from the EU, Japan and South Korea, 10% from the UK within its quota, 25% on the non-U.S. content of USMCA vehicles, 127.5% for a Chinese EV. ATVs and small vehicles up to 1,000 cc, golf carts and snowmobiles are outside the auto action but carry the Section 232 metals duty.

productGroups.label: Trucks and pickups: light trucks, heavy trucks, dump trucks
productGroups.blurb: Trucks for goods: pickups and light trucks pay the 25% "chicken tax" base rate (Korea too), plus the Section 232 automobile duty (25%; the EU, Japan and Korea pay only the 25% base). Trucks over 5 t pay 25% (4% for cab chassis) plus the 25% Section 232 truck duty; off-highway dumpers are Free plus 25%.

productGroups.label: Special-purpose vehicles: mobile cranes, fire trucks, concrete mixers, wreckers
productGroups.blurb: Special-purpose vehicles are Free at base. Mobile cranes and drilling rigs carry the Section 232 metals duty on mobile equipment (25%, 15% for deal partners); concrete mixers and other special trucks the 25% Section 232 truck duty; fire trucks only the Section 301 duty for the country.

productGroups.label: Chassis fitted with engines
productGroups.blurb: Chassis with engines pay Free to 4% at base. Chassis for cars are Section 232 auto parts (25%); chassis for trucks, road tractors and buses are Section 232 truck vehicles or parts (25%).

productGroups.label: Vehicle bodies and cabs
productGroups.blurb: Bodies and cabs pay 2.5% (cars) or 4% (trucks and buses), Free for farm tractors. Car bodies are Section 232 auto parts and truck cabs truck parts (25%) when they are parts of those vehicles.

productGroups.label: Auto parts: bumpers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, radiators, steering, airbags
productGroups.blurb: Auto parts pay 2.5% or Free at base. Most of 8708 is on the Section 232 parts lists: 25% when the article is a part of a passenger vehicle or light truck (15% in total from the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan, 10% from the UK, Free under USMCA) and 25% when it is a truck or bus part. AD/CVD deposits apply to Chinese steel wheels and Chinese and Turkish brake drums.

productGroups.label: Works trucks for factories, warehouses and airports (tugs, tow tractors)
productGroups.blurb: Works trucks (factory, warehouse and airport tugs and tow tractors) are Free at base; complete works trucks carry the 25% Section 232 truck duty and their parts the truck-parts duty when used in such vehicles.

productGroups.label: Tanks and armored fighting vehicles
productGroups.blurb: Tanks and other armored fighting vehicles and their parts are Free at base; only the Section 301 duty for the country applies.

productGroups.label: Motorcycles, scooters, mopeds and e-bikes
productGroups.blurb: Motorcycles, scooters and mopeds are Free up to 700 cc and 2.4% above; electric motorcycles and e-bikes (8711.60) are Free. Products of China pay 25% (List 2: e-bikes and electric motorcycles; List 1: over 800 cc) or 7.5% (List 4A) plus 12.5%. Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc are banned from importation since September 29, 2026.

productGroups.label: Bicycles and other non-motorized cycles
productGroups.blurb: Bicycles pay 11%, or 5.5% for light road bikes (under 16.3 kg with narrow tires, 8712.00.25) and certain wheel sizes (8712.00.44); other cycles 3.7%. Chinese bicycles add 25% (List 3) and 12.5%.

productGroups.label: Wheelchairs and mobility carriages
productGroups.blurb: Wheelchairs and mobility carriages, manual or powered, are Free at base; only the Section 301 duty for the country applies.

productGroups.label: Parts of motorcycles, bicycles and wheelchairs
productGroups.blurb: Motorcycle and wheelchair parts are Free; bicycle parts pay Free to 10%: frames 3.9%, frame tubing sets 6%, rims 5%, saddles and pedals 8%, spokes and some hubs, brakes and crank-gear 10%; derailleurs, cotterless cranksets, sprockets and caliper brakes Free.

productGroups.label: Baby carriages, strollers and parts
productGroups.blurb: Baby carriages, strollers and their parts pay 4.4%, plus the Section 301 duty for the country (Chinese strollers 12.5%).

productGroups.label: Trailers, semi-trailers, campers, container chassis, hand trucks and carts
productGroups.blurb: Trailers and semi-trailers are Free at base; most carry the 25% Section 232 metals duty (campers, van and platform trailers, container chassis). Hand trucks and carts pay 3.2%, trailer parts 3.1%, castors 5.7%, plus 25%. Chassis, van-type trailers, steel trailer wheels and hand trucks also face AD/CVD orders.

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.title: A new electric car from China: 127.5%
workedExamples.body: Base rate **2.5%**. China pays **+100%** under the 2024 Section 301 increase on electric vehicles (9903.91.03, U.S. note 31(d)) and **+25%** Section 232 on automobiles (9903.94.01); note 33(a) adds any other Chapter 99 duty on top. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty on China does not apply to Section 232 vehicles (note 52(f)(2)). Total **127.5%**: on a $40,000 car, **$51,000** in duty. The battery pack shipped on its own is classified in Chapter 85.

workedExamples.title: A gasoline car from Japan, Germany or South Korea: 15%
workedExamples.body: The 2.5% base rate is below 15%, so the deal headings set the total at **15%** (9903.94.41 Japan, 9903.94.51 EU, 9903.94.61 South Korea; U.S. notes 33(k), (n), (s) and (m)). No 2026 Section 301 floor and no Section 232 metals duty are added (notes 52(f)(2), 33(k)(1)). On a $30,000 car: **$4,500**. For Korea a KORUS (Free) claim still totals 15%.

workedExamples.title: A USMCA car from Mexico: 25% on the non-U.S. content
workedExamples.body: With a USMCA claim (SPI "S") the 2.5% base is Free and the Section 232 duty is **25% of the non-U.S. content** (9903.94.03, note 33(d)). U.S. content is the value of parts wholly obtained, produced entirely or substantially transformed in the United States, and only counts once the Secretary of Commerce approves the importer's documentation; the U.S. content is entered on a second line under 9903.94.02 at 0% (CSMS # 65649652). A $30,000 car with $12,000 of approved U.S. content pays 25% × $18,000 = **$4,500** (15% of the value). With no approval: 25% of $30,000 = $7,500; with no USMCA claim: 27.5%.

workedExamples.title: A UK car inside and outside the quota: 10% or 27.5%
workedExamples.body: Inside the UK tariff-rate quota (100,000 passenger vehicles a year, at most 25,000 a quarter plus carry-forward) the 2.5% base plus **7.5%** (9903.94.31, note 33(i)) makes **10%**: $3,000 on a $30,000 car. Once CBP reports the quota filled, the car pays 2.5% + 25% (9903.94.01) = 27.5%. UK pickups and other light trucks have no quota.

workedExamples.title: A pickup truck: the 25% base rate decides it
workedExamples.body: Light trucks up to 5 t G.V.W. pay a **25%** base rate (the "chicken tax"; KORUS keeps 25% for Korea). From Japan, the EU or Korea the deal rate is a 15% floor, so the total stays **25%** (9903.94.40, 9903.94.50, 9903.94.60). From Thailand or another country without a deal: 25% + 25% Section 232 = **50%** — $15,000 on a $30,000 pickup. A USMCA pickup from Mexico pays 25% only on its non-U.S. content.

workedExamples.title: An axle for cars from Mexico: 27.5% or Free
workedExamples.body: Drive axles for vehicles of 8703 are on the note 33(g) parts list. Without a USMCA claim: 2.5% + **25%** (9903.94.05) = 27.5%, $2,750 on $10,000 (no 10% Mexico Section 301 duty, note 52(f)(3)). With a USMCA claim the part enters under 9903.94.06: **Free**. If the same axle is for a tractor, not a car or light truck, it is not an auto part: the base rate plus the Section 301 duty for the country applies instead.

workedExamples.title: A heavy road tractor from Mexico under USMCA
workedExamples.body: Road tractors for semi-trailers are medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (note 38(b)). With USMCA, the 4% base is Free and the duty is 25% of the non-U.S. content (9903.74.03, note 38(d); CSMS # 68559236): $150,000 with $50,000 of approved U.S. content pays **$25,000**. Without USMCA: 4% + 25% (9903.74.01) = 29%, $43,500. Buses get no content rule: +10% on the full value (9903.74.02).

workedExamples.title: A bicycle and an e-bike from China
workedExamples.body: A standard adult bicycle pays **11%** base + 25% China Section 301 (List 3, 9903.88.03) + 12.5% 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.31) = **48.5%**. An e-bike with a motor up to 250 W (8711.60.00.50) is Free at base and pays 25% (9903.88.02) + 12.5% = **37.5%**. From Vietnam the same bicycle pays 11% + 12.5% = 23.5%.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover railway or tramway rolling stock designed solely for running on rails.

**Note 2.** For the purposes of this chapter, "tractors" means vehicles constructed essentially for hauling or pushing another vehicle, appliance or load, whether or not they contain subsidiary provision for the transport, in connection with the main use of the tractor, of tools, seeds, fertilizers or other goods. Machines and working tools designed for fitting to tractors of heading 8701 as interchangeable equipment remain classified in their respective headings even if presented with the tractor, and whether or not mounted on it.

**Note 3.** Motor chassis fitted with cabs fall in headings 8702 to 8704, and not in heading 8706.

**Note 4.** Heading 8712 includes all children's bicycles. Other children's cycles fall in heading 9503.

**Subheading note 1.** Subheading 8708.22.00 covers: (a) front windscreens (windshields), rear windows and other windows, framed; and (b) front windscreens (windshields), rear windows and other windows, whether or not framed, incorporating heating devices or other electrical or electronic devices, when suitable for use solely or principally with the motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**1.** Road tractors, trailers and semi-trailers remain separately classified in headings 8701 and 8716, respectively, even when entered together.

**2.** For the purposes of classifying bicycles under the provisions therefor in heading 8712, the diameter of each wheel is the diameter measured to the outer circumference of the tire which is mounted thereon or, if none is mounted thereon, of the usual tire for such wheel.

**Statistical note 1.** For the purposes of statistical reporting numbers in headings 8701 and 8703, report as "new" only those motor vehicles that have been produced or assembled but have not been sold to any person or entity other than a manufacturer, distributor or dealer. Report as "used" only those motor vehicles the equitable or legal title to which has been transferred via a first sale by a manufacturer, distributor or dealer to an ultimate purchaser.

seo.shortDescription: Every U.S. tariff change on cars, auto parts, trucks, buses, motorcycles and bicycles since 2025, dated and sourced: the Section 232 auto, parts and truck duties, the 15% EU, Japan and Korea deals, the UK quota, the USMCA U.S.-content rule, China's 100% EV duty, the 2026 Section 301 and Canada Section 338 duties, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and AD/CVD orders.

tariffUpdates.intro: What changed for imported vehicles and parts, when, and under which document. The top of the page lists every extra duty in force today for each country, with its Chapter 99 heading and the exemptions that matter; below it, a dated change log (newest first) runs from the 2025 IEEPA tariffs and the Section 232 automobile actions to the October 2026 schedule, including the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on chassis, trailers, wheels, brake drums and golf carts. The base rates of the 402 lines are compared between the 2025 Basic Edition and the 2026 Revision 21.
tariffUpdates.scope: U.S. import duties on Chapter 87 goods: base rates (General, Special, Column 2), the Chapter 99 duties in force on 2026-10-13 — Section 232 (automobiles, auto parts, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and buses, their parts, and steel, aluminum and copper), the 2026 Section 301 duties on 60 economies, the Brazil and China Section 301 duties, the Canada Section 338 duty and import ban, and the Russia rates — for the countries in the rate matrix and the rest of the world. Ended measures (IEEPA, Section 122) are kept in the log. AD/CVD orders are explained in the log; their company-specific rates are not in the totals.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 (steel, aluminum, copper) + Section 232 (passenger vehicles and light trucks) + Section 232 (medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and buses)
inEffect.exemption: These are the USMCA headings. A USMCA-qualifying passenger vehicle or light truck pays 25% only on the value of its non-U.S. content (9903.94.03, U.S. note 33(d)), and a USMCA medium- or heavy-duty truck the same (9903.74.03, note 38(d)), once the Secretary of Commerce approves the importer's U.S.-content documentation; the U.S. content is entered on a second line under 9903.94.02 or 9903.74.06 at 0% (CSMS # 65649652, # 68559236). U.S. content is the value of parts wholly obtained, produced entirely or substantially transformed in the United States. Without an approval the 25% applies to the full value. USMCA parts of cars and trucks pay no Section 232 duty (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10). Buses get no content rule (+10%, 9903.74.02). Mobile industrial equipment (single-axle and track-laying tractors, mobile cranes) under the metals action pays 25% on the non-U.S. content and on U.S. content above 40% of the value (9903.82.20 / 9903.82.21) through 2027. Relief: articles that are not cars, light trucks or MHDVs and vehicles 25 or more years old (9903.94.02, 9903.94.04, 9903.74.05, 9903.74.07). The 2025 IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico never reached Section 232 autos and parts (U.S. note 33(a)(2)–(3)) and ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A USMCA $40,000 SUV from Mexico or Canada with $16,000 of approved U.S. content pays 25% × $24,000 = $6,000 (15% of the value); without an approval, $10,000. A USMCA engine part or axle pays nothing; a USMCA bus pays 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Goods of Mexico entered free under USMCA are exempt (note 52(h), 9903.05.94). Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)). The 25% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Mexican goods (9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Only non-USMCA Mexican goods outside the Section 232 actions pay +10%: motorcycles 10%, bicycles 21% (11% base), wheelchairs, strollers, bicycle parts and listed articles that are not vehicle parts. Claiming USMCA removes it.

inEffect.country: Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria and 33 more
inEffect.exemption: Mobile industrial equipment of note 16(c)(xi) — single-axle and track-laying tractors, mobile cranes and drilling derricks — from the deal partners (the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Argentina, Ecuador, El Salvador and Guatemala) pays 15% in total, or nothing extra when the base rate is 15% or more (9903.82.22), through December 31, 2027; from January 1, 2028 it pays 25% (Proclamation 11032). Relief: no metal (9903.82.01), metal under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03), motorcycle parts for U.S. manufacturing (9903.82.13). Goods under 9903.82 do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duties (notes 52(f)(1), 50(a)(vi)(1)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A German or Japanese mobile crane, Free at base, pays 15%: $150,000 on $1 million. From 2028 it is scheduled to pay 25%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 232 (passenger vehicles and light trucks) + Section 232 (automobile parts)
inEffect.now: 12.5% (in place of base) + 15% (in place of base) or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Passenger vehicles and light trucks (note 33(k)) and the listed auto parts (note 33(l)) of Japan pay 15% in total when the column 1 rate is under 15% (9903.94.41, 9903.94.43), and only the base rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.40, 9903.94.42), since September 16, 2025 (Executive Order 14345; 90 FR 44638). They do not pay the 2026 Section 301 or metals duties (notes 52(f)(2)–(3), 33(k)(1)). Importers who certify that other parts are for U.S. vehicle production or repair can enter them at 15% in total (9903.94.54 / 9903.94.55, note 33(r)). Trucks over 5 t, buses and truck parts get no Japan rate. Everything else pays the 12.5% Section 301 rate in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.49). The 15% IEEPA reciprocal rate ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $30,000 Japanese car pays $4,500 (15%); a Japanese pickup keeps its 25% base rate; a car part 15%; a motorcycle, bicycle or a part that is not a vehicle part 12.5%; a heavy truck its base rate + 25%. A 25-year-old import pays 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Goods of Canada entered free under USMCA are exempt from the 10% (note 52(g), 9903.05.93), and Section 232 goods are exempt (note 52(f)). The 50% Section 338 duty (9903.03.14, U.S. note 51) has no USMCA exemption and, since September 15, 2026, applies in addition to any Section 232 duty (Proclamation 11065; note 51(c) now relieves only 9903.03.13). In Chapter 87 it covers golf carts and similar vehicles (8703.10.50) and vehicles up to 1,000 cc (8703.21.01). Motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50) paid it from August 22, 2026 and have been excluded from importation since September 29, 2026 (Proclamation 11063). The 35% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA cars, trucks and parts from Canada pay only the Section 232 content duty; a Canadian golf cart pays 75% (25% metals + 50%), a Canadian side-by-side or other vehicle up to 1,000 cc 65% (15% + 50%), and large Canadian motorcycles cannot be imported.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 232 (passenger vehicles and light trucks) + Section 232 (automobile parts)
inEffect.now: 12.5% (in place of base) + 15% (in place of base) or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Passenger vehicles and light trucks (note 33(s)) and listed auto parts (note 33(t)) of South Korea pay 15% in total when the rate is under 15% (9903.94.61, 9903.94.63) and only that rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.60, 9903.94.62), since November 1, 2025 (90 FR 55964). Under note 33(m) the comparison uses the column 1-General rate or a KORUS (KR) rate properly claimed, so a KORUS car (Free) still pays 15% and a pickup keeps the 25% KORUS rate. Certified parts for U.S. production or repair: 9903.94.64 / 9903.94.65. No 2026 Section 301 or metals duty on these (notes 52(f)(2)–(3)). Other goods pay the 12.5% rate in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.71). The IEEPA reciprocal rate ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $30,000 Korean car pays $4,500 (15%) with or without a KORUS claim; Korean auto parts 15%; Korean trucks over 5 t their base rate + 25%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 232 (passenger vehicles and light trucks) + Section 232 (automobile parts)
inEffect.now: 10% (in place of base) + 15% (in place of base) or 10% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Passenger vehicles and light trucks (note 33(n)) and listed auto parts (note 33(o)) of the 27 EU member states pay 15% in total when the column 1 rate is under 15% (9903.94.51, 9903.94.53) and only the base rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.50, 9903.94.52), since August 1, 2025 (90 FR 46136). Certified parts for U.S. production or repair: 9903.94.44 / 9903.94.45. No 2026 Section 301 or metals duty on these (notes 52(f)(2)–(3)). Other EU goods pay 10% in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.38–9903.05.39); no Chapter 87 line is on the EU exception list of note 52(j)(2). The IEEPA rate ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $50,000 German, Italian or Swedish car pays $7,500 (15%); an EU pickup 25%; listed EU auto parts 15%; heavy trucks their base rate + 25%; EU motorcycles and e-bikes 10%; bicycles 11% (their base rate is above 10%).

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 301 (China, 2018-2019 lists) + Section 301 (China, 2024 four-year review)
inEffect.exemption: The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.31) does not apply to Section 232 vehicles, parts, trucks and metals goods (note 52(f)); the China duties of notes 20 and 31 do, on top of Section 232 (note 33(a)). Note 31(d), 9903.91.03: +100% on electric and plug-in hybrid cars (8703.60–8703.90) and electric buses (8702.40, 8702.90) since September 27, 2024. List 1 (9903.88.01, 25%): gasoline and diesel cars and conventional hybrids (8703.21–8703.50), trucks, buses, motorcycles over 800 cc, works trucks. List 2 (9903.88.02, 25%): road and farm tractors, cranes, electric trucks, e-bikes and electric motorcycles, mopeds up to 50 cc. List 3 (9903.88.03, 25%): auto parts, chassis and bodies, bicycles and their parts, trailers and hand trucks. List 4A (9903.88.15, 7.5%): snowmobiles and golf carts, motorcycles of 50–800 cc and their parts, tanks. Exclusions through November 9, 2026 (9903.88.69, note 20(vvv)): mopeds up to 50 cc valued up to $500, certain park-gear blanks and stator shafts (8708.40.75.70), certain bicycle trailers (8716.40). From November 10, 2026 intermodal chassis and their parts add +100% (9903.91.12, note 31(k)). USTR continued the 2018 actions (91 FR 64212). The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Chinese EV pays 127.5% (2.5% + 100% + 25%); a gasoline car 52.5%; a car part 52.5% (2.5% + 25% List 3 + 25% Section 232); a bicycle 48.5%; an e-bike 37.5%; a golf cart 35% plus AD/CVD deposits. AD/CVD orders also cover Chinese chassis, steel wheels, brake drums, hand trucks and van-type trailers.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 232 (steel, aluminum, copper) + Section 232 (passenger vehicles and light trucks) + Section 232 (automobile parts) + Section 232 (medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts)
inEffect.now: 10% (in place of base) + +35% or 10% (in place of base) + +10% or +10% or +17.5% or 10% (in place of base) + +25% or 10% (in place of base) or +15%
inEffect.exemption: UK passenger vehicles of the 12 subheadings in note 33(i) pay 7.5% on top of the 2.5% base (10% in all) within a tariff-rate quota of 100,000 vehicles a year — no more than 25,000 a quarter, with unused quantity carried from Q1 to Q3 and Q2 to Q4 — (9903.94.31, since June 30, 2025); over the quota, 25% (9903.94.01). UK light trucks have no quota and pay 25%. The UK auto parts listed in note 33(j) (98 Chapter 87 lines) pay 10% in all (9903.94.32), and other UK parts certified for UK-built automobiles 10% (9903.94.33, note 33(q)). These pay no 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(2)–(3)). UK trucks, buses and truck parts pay the general Section 232 rates. Metals derivatives pay 25% (15% with at least 95% UK-melted metal, 9903.82.05). Other UK goods: +10% (9903.05.81); no Chapter 87 line is on the UK exception list (note 52(j)(1)). The 10% IEEPA tariff ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $50,000 UK car inside the quota pays $5,000; once CBP reports the quota filled, $13,750 (27.5%). Listed UK car parts pay 10%; UK bicycles 21%; motorcycles 10% or 12.4%.

inEffect.now: 10% (in place of base) + 15% (in place of base) or 10% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Listed auto parts of Taiwan (notes 33(g), 33(u)) pay 15% in total when the column 1 rate is under 15% (9903.94.67) and only the base rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.66), since May 1, 2026 (91 FR 31818); certified parts for U.S. production or repair: 9903.94.68 / 9903.94.69. Taiwan has no vehicle deal: its cars and light trucks pay 25% (9903.94.01). Other goods pay 10% in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.76). Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese car parts pay 15%; bicycles keep their 11% base (10% floor for lower-rated bicycles and parts); a Taiwanese car pays 27.5%.

inEffect.exemption: +12.5% on products of Thailand (9903.05.77). Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)). Thailand has no Section 232 deal rate. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026; Section 232 vehicles and parts were outside both.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Thai pickup pays 25% + 25% = 50%; Thai car parts 27.5%; motorcycles 12.5%. Thai chassis pay AD (72.85% for most exporters) and CVD (10.50%) deposits.

inEffect.exemption: +10% on products of India (9903.05.44). Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)). India has no Section 232 deal rate. The extra 25% IEEPA duty on India ended February 7, 2026 and the reciprocal duty February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian cars pay 27.5%, car parts 25% + base, motorcycles 10% or 12.4%, bicycles 21%.

inEffect.exemption: +12.5% on products of Vietnam (9903.05.84). Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)). Vietnam has no Section 232 deal rate. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026; Section 232 vehicles and parts were outside both.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese cars pay 27.5%, car parts 2.5% + 25%, bicycles 11% + 12.5% = 23.5%, e-bikes and motorcycles 12.5%. Vietnamese chassis pay a 186.84% AD deposit, and Commerce is checking whether Vietnamese steel wheels circumvent the China wheel orders.

inEffect.exemption: +25% Brazil Section 301 (9903.05.01, since July 22, 2026) plus +12.5% 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.27). Both are lifted for the Section 232 vehicles, parts, trucks and metals goods (notes 50(a)(vi), 52(f); 9903.05.07, 9903.05.90). No Chapter 87 line is on the Brazil exemption list (note 50(a)(ii)). Brazil's 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A Brazilian car pays 27.5% (Section 232 only); a Brazilian motorcycle or bicycle 37.5% plus its base rate.

inEffect.exemption: Belarus, Cuba and North Korea (no normal trade relations, general note 3(b)) pay column 2 rates and +25% on the agricultural and industrial equipment of note 16(c)(ix)–(x) (9903.82.12) instead of the 15% the others pay.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Farm tractors and their parts from these countries pay the column 2 rate + 25%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies) + Section 232 (aluminum, Russia) + Section 232 (steel, aluminum, copper) + Russia (rates in lieu of column 2)
inEffect.now: +12.5% or 35% (in place of base) + +12.5% or +10% or +25% or 35% (in place of base) + +10% or 35% (in place of base) + +212.5% or 35% (in place of base) + +25% or +212.5%
inEffect.exemption: Russia pays column 2 rates (since April 9, 2022) and, on the note 30(b) lines, 35% in lieu of column 2 (9903.90.08). Russian aluminum derivatives pay 200% (9903.85.68); steel and copper derivatives 25% (9903.82.16). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.66) is lifted for Section 232 goods (note 52(f)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian vehicles and parts face column 2 or 35% rates plus the Section 232 duties, and 200% on aluminum derivative articles: imports are effectively priced out.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (47: Algeria, Angola, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Bahrain, Bangladesh, Cambodia, …)
inEffect.exemption: +10% or +12.5% for the other listed economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.83), or a floor in place of a lower base rate where the heading says so. Goods under the Section 232 vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings do not pay it (U.S. note 52(f), 9903.05.90); no Chapter 87 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or a country exception list (note 52(j)). The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026; Section 232 vehicles and parts were outside both.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Their cars pay 2.5% + 25%, car parts their base + 25%, motorcycles, bicycles and other goods the base rate + 10% or 12.5%.

inEffect.country: All countries except Russia, Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Switzerland, Cyprus, Czechia, Germany, Denmark, Ecuador, Estonia, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Guatemala, Croatia, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden, Slovenia, Slovakia, El Salvador, Taiwan, Belarus, Cuba, North Korea
inEffect.now: +10% or 10% (in place of base) or 15% (in place of base) or +25%
inEffect.exemption: The steel, aluminum and copper action (U.S. note 16) reaches 88 Chapter 87 lines: derivative articles such as bumpers (8708.10), trailers and semi-trailers (8716.10, 8716.39), hand trucks and carts (8716.80.50), castors and trailer parts (8716.90), golf carts and snowmobiles (8703.10) at 25% (9903.82.09); mobile industrial equipment at 25% (15% for deal partners, USMCA content rule) through 2027; farm tractors, vehicles up to 1,000 cc and other agricultural and industrial equipment at 15% in total (9903.82.10). Since April 6, 2026 the duty is charged on the full customs value regardless of metal content (Proclamation 11021). Lower rates: 10% with at least 85% U.S.-melted metal (9903.82.06 / 9903.82.07); UK 15% with 95% UK metal. Relief: no metal (9903.82.01), metal under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03), motorcycle parts for U.S. manufacturing (9903.82.13). Section 232 cars, auto parts, trucks and truck parts are not subject to it (notes 33(a)(1), 33(f)(1), 38).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $10,000 steel bumper that is not an auto part, or a $20,000 utility trailer, pays 25% on top of its base rate from any country (China adds its Section 301 list duty). The 2026 Section 301 and Brazil duties are not added.

inEffect.country: All countries except Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, Germany, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, Finland, France, Greece, Croatia, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden, Slovenia, Slovakia
inEffect.exemption: Passenger vehicles (sedans, SUVs, crossovers, minivans, cargo vans) and light trucks of the 17 note 33(b) subheadings (74 lines) pay +25% since April 3, 2025 (Proclamation 10908), new or used, also when an FTA rate is claimed. Instead: the EU, Japan and South Korea 15% in total (9903.94.41, .51, .61); the UK 10% within its quota (9903.94.31); USMCA vehicles 25% of the non-U.S. content (9903.94.03). Relief: an article of these subheadings that is not a passenger vehicle or light truck (9903.94.02; an electric truck of 8704.60 over the light-truck class pays the truck duty instead), and a vehicle made in a year at least 25 years before the year of entry (9903.94.04). These entries pay no metals, Canada or Mexico IEEPA, 2026 Section 301 or Brazil duty (notes 33(a)(1)–(3), 52(f)(2), 50(a)(vi)); AD/CVD and the China duties stack. Vehicles under 1,000 cc, golf carts and snowmobiles (8703.10, 8703.21) are outside the action.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $30,000 car from Vietnam, Thailand, India, Brazil or Taiwan pays $8,250 (27.5%); a pickup from those countries 50%. A 25-year-old classic pays its base rate plus the Section 301 duty for its country.

inEffect.country: All countries except Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, Germany, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, Finland, France, Greece, Croatia, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Latvia, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Sweden, Slovenia, Slovakia, Taiwan
inEffect.exemption: Auto parts on the note 33(g) list (130 provisions across chapters 40, 70, 73, 83–85, 87, 90 and 94; 119 Chapter 87 lines) pay +25% since May 3, 2025 (Proclamation 10908), but only when they are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks; the same articles for other uses enter under 9903.94.06 (note 33(h)(ii)). USMCA parts, other than knock-down kits, enter free of it (9903.94.06, note 33(h)(i)). Japan, the EU, South Korea and Taiwan: 15% in total; UK: 10% in total. Since November 1, 2025 an importer may also certify that other parts will be used for U.S. vehicle production or repair and enter them under 9903.94.07 at 25% (an election under Proclamation 10984, not in chapters 72, 73 or 76), in place of the metals and 2026 Section 301 duties. U.S. assemblers can claim an import adjustment offset (Proclamation 10925). No 2026 Section 301 duty on these parts (note 52(f)(3)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $10,000 brake caliper or axle for cars pays $2,750 from Thailand, India or Brazil, $1,500 from Japan or Germany, $1,000 from the UK (if listed in 33(j)) and nothing from Mexico or Canada under USMCA.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 (medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and buses)
inEffect.exemption: Medium- and heavy-duty vehicles of note 38(b) (58 lines: road tractors 8701.21–8701.29, trucks over 5 t and dumpers of 8704, electric and other trucks 8704.60 / 8704.90, concrete mixers and other special vehicles 8705.40 / 8705.90, chassis for them, works trucks 8709.11 / 8709.19) pay +25%, and buses of 8702 (10 lines) +10%, since November 1, 2025 (Proclamation 10984). No country deal rates. USMCA trucks: 25% of the non-U.S. content (9903.74.03); USMCA buses still pay 10% on the full value. Relief: not an MHDV (9903.74.05), 25 years or older (9903.74.07). No 2026 Section 301, metals or Canada / Mexico IEEPA duty (notes 52(f)(5), 38(a)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $150,000 road tractor pays 29% (4% + 25%) from any country without USMCA, including the EU and Japan; a $300,000 coach pays 12%.

inEffect.exemption: Parts of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles on the note 38(i) list (182 provisions; 99 Chapter 87 lines) pay +25% since November 1, 2025 (9903.74.08), only when they are parts of such vehicles; the listed articles for other uses enter under 9903.74.11. USMCA parts: no duty (9903.74.10). Importers may elect to certify other parts for U.S. MHDV production or repair (9903.74.09, note 38(j)). The UK, EU, Japan and Korea deal rates do not cover truck parts. No 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)(6)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $10,000 truck axle or brake drum pays $2,750 (2.5% + 25%) from any country without USMCA; Chinese and Turkish brake drums add AD/CVD deposits.

changes.title: Chapter 87 base rates: 2025 Basic Edition vs 2026 Revision 21
changes.detail: 396 of 402 lines keep the same General, Special and Column 2 rates. New or renumbered statistical lines: 8707.10.00.30, 8707.10.00.90, 8708.29.51.50, 8708.29.51.90, 8708.80.16.10, 8708.80.16.90. The base rates themselves did not move: cars 2.5%, light trucks 25%, parts 2.5% or Free.

changes.title: China Section 301 lists continue after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 87 this keeps 25% (Lists 1–3) and 7.5% (List 4A) on Chinese vehicles, parts, bicycles and trailers, on top of Section 232.

changes.title: Chinese chassis AD/CVD orders: expedited sunset reviews
changes.detail: Commerce found that revoking the 2021 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on chassis and subassemblies from China would likely lead to renewed dumping (188.05% China-wide) and subsidies, and the ITC scheduled expedited five-year reviews. The orders on container and other trailer chassis (8716.39.00.90, 8716.90.50) stay in force during the reviews.

changes.title: Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc banned from importation
changes.detail: Proclamation 11063 excluded certain Canadian products that carried the Section 338 duty from importation, for goods imported from 12:01 a.m. ET on September 29, 2026; in Chapter 87 this covers motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50). Goods imported earlier but not yet entered pay the 50% duty.

changes.title: Brake drums: compacted graphite iron drums found to circumvent the orders
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily determined that compacted graphite iron brake drums from China are later-developed merchandise circumventing the 2025 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on brake drums, so they would pay the same deposits.

changes.title: Canada Section 338: 50% extended to golf carts and small vehicles, on top of Section 232
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 (signed September 8, 2026) revised the Section 338 list effective September 15, 2026: it added golf carts and similar vehicles (8703.10.50) and vehicles up to 1,000 cc (8703.21.01) to heading 9903.03.14 and made the 50% apply in addition to any Section 232 duty. The duty applies to USMCA goods too (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Antidumping order on Chinese hand trucks continued
changes.detail: After the fourth sunset review, Commerce continued the antidumping duty order on hand trucks and certain parts from China (8716.80.50.10, 8716.80.50.90, 8716.90.50.60) for five more years.

changes.title: Van-type trailers from China, Mexico and Canada: AD/CVD investigations
changes.detail: Commerce made final affirmative determinations on van-type trailers and subassemblies from China (antidumping 130.86%, cash deposit 129.73%; countervailing 134.75%) and preliminary antidumping determinations on Mexico (8.72% for most exporters, 79.92% for two) and Canada (4.29%, 44.86% for two), plus a preliminary countervailing duty on Mexico (1.91%). Deposits are being collected; orders follow only if the ITC makes final affirmative injury votes (hearing held August 27, 2026). The Canadian countervailing duty case was withdrawn.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty takes effect: motorcycles over 800 cc
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 (signed July 20, 2026) imposed 50% on listed Canadian products to offset Canada's motor-vehicle tariff scheme; after a three-day suspension (Proclamation 11056) it took effect on August 22, 2026. In Chapter 87 it reached motorcycles over 800 cc (8711.50). Articles subject to Section 232 were exempt until September 14 (9903.03.15).

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 duties on 60 economies; Section 232 vehicles and parts exempt
changes.detail: +10% or +12.5% (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) on products of 60 economies from July 24, 2026, listed against all 402 Chapter 87 lines. Note 52(f) (9903.05.90) lifts them for goods under the Section 232 headings — passenger vehicles and light trucks, listed auto parts, trucks, buses, truck parts and metals goods — so in practice they reach motorcycles, e-bikes, bicycles, wheelchairs, strollers, some trailers and listed articles that are not vehicle parts. For the EU (10%), Japan and South Korea (12.5%) and Taiwan (10%) the rate replaces a lower base rate. Canadian and Mexican goods entered under USMCA are exempt (notes 52(g)–(h)).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Brazil Section 301: 25%; Section 232 vehicles and parts exempt
changes.detail: +25% on products of Brazil (9903.05.01) from July 22, 2026, on top of the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty from July 24. Note 50(a)(vi) (9903.05.07) lifts it for the Section 232 vehicles, parts, trucks, buses and metals goods, the same list as note 52(f).

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims still lower the Section 232 vehicle duty to the non-U.S. content and remove it on parts.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on chassis from Mexico, Thailand and Vietnam
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping orders on chassis and subassemblies from Mexico (32.37%), Thailand (72.85%; 129.63% for one exporter) and Vietnam (186.84%) and countervailing orders on Mexico (76.91%) and Thailand (10.50%; 9.65%–10.72% for named exporters), after the ITC's affirmative injury votes. They cover chassis of 8716.39.00.90 and subassemblies of 8716.90.50.

changes.title: Section 232 metals: new rates for mobile, agricultural and industrial equipment
changes.detail: Proclamation 11032 set new rates from June 8, 2026 for the equipment lists of note 16(c)(ix)–(xi): mobile industrial equipment (single-axle and track-laying tractors, mobile cranes, drilling derricks) pays 25% (9903.82.09), 15% in total from the deal partners (9903.82.22) and, under USMCA, 25% on the non-U.S. content plus U.S. content above 40% (9903.82.20) through December 31, 2027; agricultural and industrial equipment, including farm tractors, vehicles up to 1,000 cc of 8703.21, farm wagons and agricultural tractor parts, pays 15% in total (9903.82.10). A derivative counts as U.S.-made at 85% U.S.-melted metal (10%).

changes.title: Equipment lines leave the general 25% metals heading
changes.detail: From April 6 to June 7, 2026 the farm, industrial and mobile equipment entries of Chapter 87 (tractors, cranes, vehicles of 8703.21, agricultural tractor parts) paid the general 25% under 9903.82.09. Proclamation 11032 moved them to the equipment lists from June 8, 2026, with the 15% and 25% rates above.

changes.title: Taiwan: listed auto parts at 15% in total
changes.detail: Listed Taiwanese auto parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.67) or their base rate when higher (9903.94.66), for goods entered from May 1, 2026 (91 FR 31818). Taiwanese vehicles stay at 25%.

changes.title: Scheduled: equipment metals rates rise to 25% on January 1, 2028
changes.detail: Under Proclamations 11021 and 11032, the 15% totals for agricultural and industrial equipment and for the deal partners' mobile equipment, and the USMCA content rule for mobile equipment, end December 31, 2027; from January 1, 2028 these Chapter 87 lines pay 25% (UK 15% with 95% UK metal, 10% with 85% U.S.-melted metal). The HTS heading for the step is not published yet.

changes.title: Section 232 metals rebuilt on full value (Proclamation 11021)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the earlier steel and aluminum headings with 9903.82.02–9903.82.26, charged on the full customs value regardless of metal content. Chapter 87 derivatives — bumpers, trailers, hand trucks, castors and trailer parts, golf carts and snowmobiles — pay 25% (9903.82.09); UK goods with at least 95% UK-melted metal 15% (9903.82.05); goods made from U.S.-melted metal 10%. Section 232 vehicles and auto and truck parts remain outside the metals duties.

changes.title: Steel wheels: circumvention inquiry on Vietnam
changes.detail: Commerce opened a country-wide inquiry into whether steel wheels from Vietnam circumvent the 2019 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on certain steel wheels (22.5 and 24.5 inch truck and trailer wheels) from China.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. Section 232 cars, light trucks, auto parts, trucks, truck parts and metals goods were exempt (9903.03.06), as were USMCA-qualifying goods of Canada and Mexico. Motorcycles, bicycles, e-bikes and other non-Section 232 goods paid it.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. Importers can claim refunds of IEEPA duties paid. The 9903.01 and 9903.02 headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026; the 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24. Indian Section 232 vehicles and parts were never subject to either.

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), on every Chapter 87 line. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. Note 33(a) did not exempt Section 232 vehicles and parts from it, as it did for the Canada and Mexico duties. It ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: South Korea: cars and light trucks at 15% in total
changes.detail: Korean passenger vehicles and light trucks pay 15% in total when the column 1-General or KORUS rate is under 15% (9903.94.61), and only that rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.60), for goods entered from November 1, 2025, replacing the 25% (9903.94.01). Published December 4, 2025 (90 FR 55964).

changes.title: Korean auto parts at 15%; certified-parts election opens
changes.detail: From November 1, 2025, listed Korean auto parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.63). Proclamation 10984 also let importers certify other parts for U.S. vehicle production or repair and enter them under 9903.94.07 (25%; 15% for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan deal headings, 10% under 9903.94.33 for UK parts used in UK automobiles) in place of the metals and later the 2026 Section 301 duties.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on trucks (25%) and buses (10%)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 (signed October 17, 2025) imposed 25% on medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (road tractors, trucks over 5 t, dumpers, concrete mixers, works trucks, their chassis) and 10% on buses, for goods entered from November 1, 2025, from every country. USMCA trucks pay 25% only on the non-U.S. content once Commerce approves it (9903.74.03; CSMS # 68559236); buses get no content rule.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on truck and bus parts (25%)
changes.detail: From November 1, 2025, parts of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles on the note 38(i) list (engines, transmissions, axles, brakes, wheels, seats and other parts) pay +25% (9903.74.08) when they are parts of such vehicles. USMCA parts pay nothing until Commerce sets up a non-U.S.-content process (9903.74.10).

changes.title: Scheduled: +100% on Chinese intermodal chassis from November 10, 2026
changes.detail: USTR's Section 301 action on China's maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors adds 100% on intermodal chassis, their subassemblies and parts (8716.39.00.90, 8716.90.30, 8716.90.50) of China (9903.91.12, note 31(k)). It was suspended for one year and now applies to entries from November 10, 2026; other goods of those lines enter under 9903.91.13 without it. The 25% List 3 duty and the chassis AD/CVD orders stay.

changes.title: Japan: cars and light trucks at 15% in total
changes.detail: Japanese passenger vehicles and light trucks pay 15% in total when the column 1 rate is under 15% (9903.94.41) and the base rate when it is higher (9903.94.40), from September 16, 2025, implementing Executive Order 14345 (90 FR 44638).

changes.title: Japan: listed auto parts at 15% in total
changes.detail: Listed Japanese auto parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.43), or their base rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.42), from September 16, 2025.

changes.title: Executive Order 14345 implements the U.S.-Japan agreement
changes.detail: The order set the 15% all-in rate for Japanese passenger vehicles, light trucks and listed auto parts, applied by Commerce from September 16, 2025 (see the entries for that date).

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) on top of the 25% reciprocal rate: 50% on Indian motorcycles, bicycles and other goods outside Section 232. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Russian aluminum duty (200%) reaches more Chapter 87 parts
changes.detail: The aluminum derivatives added through Commerce's inclusions process (90 FR 40326) include Chapter 87 articles, so Russian-origin ones pay 200% (9903.85.68) from August 18, 2025.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on Chinese golf carts and other low-speed vehicles
changes.detail: After the ITC's affirmative votes, Commerce issued antidumping (119.39%–312.54%; 478.09% China-wide) and countervailing (31.45%–691.58%; 41.14% all others) duty orders on low-speed personal transportation vehicles from China — golf carts, neighborhood vehicles and similar (8703.10.50, 8703.90.01) and their chassis and bodies.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on brake drums from China and Türkiye
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping (China 77.14% for listed exporters, 160.79% China-wide; Türkiye 15.22%–149.29%) and countervailing (China 11.94%–446.83%; Türkiye 2.80%–131.60%) duty orders on certain brake drums for trucks and trailers (8708.30.50).

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates from August 7, 2025 (for example Thailand and Indonesia +19%, Vietnam and Taiwan +20%, India +25%, Japan and South Korea +15%, the EU 15% in total, the UK +10%). Section 232 vehicles and parts were outside the reciprocal duties (9903.01.33), so they reached only motorcycles, bicycles, e-bikes, trailers and other goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: EU: cars and light trucks at 15% in total
changes.detail: EU passenger vehicles and light trucks pay 15% in total (9903.94.51) or their base rate when it is higher (9903.94.50), for goods entered from August 1, 2025, under the U.S.-EU framework (90 FR 46136, published September 25, 2025; earlier entries refunded).

changes.title: EU: listed auto parts at 15% in total
changes.detail: Listed EU auto parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.53) or their base rate when it is 15% or more (9903.94.52), from August 1, 2025.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Section 232 vehicles and parts were not subject to it (U.S. note 33(a)(2)). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: UK: cars at 10% within a quota
changes.detail: UK passenger vehicles of 12 subheadings pay 7.5% on top of the 2.5% base (10%) within a quota of 65,205 vehicles for the rest of 2025 and 100,000 a year from 2026 (9903.94.31), under Executive Order 14309 (90 FR 27851).

changes.title: UK: listed auto parts at 10% in total
changes.detail: UK parts in the statistical reporting numbers listed in note 33(j) pay 10% in total, including the MFN rate (9903.94.32), from June 30, 2025.

changes.title: Executive Order 14309: U.S.-UK deal on cars and parts
changes.detail: The order implementing the U.S.-UK Economic Prosperity Deal set the UK vehicle quota (100,000 a year at 10% in total) and the 10% rate on UK auto parts, applied from June 30, 2025.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. It never applied to Section 232 vehicles and parts. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on auto parts (25%)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 extended the 25% to the auto parts listed in U.S. note 33(g) — engines, transmissions, powertrain and electrical parts, chassis, bodies and most of heading 8708, plus tires, glass, batteries, lights and seats in other chapters — for goods entered from May 3, 2025, when they are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks. USMCA parts were left out (9903.94.06). Proclamation 10925 (April 29, 2025) added an import adjustment offset for U.S. vehicle assemblers.

changes.title: No stacking of the auto duty with the Canada / Mexico and metals duties
changes.detail: Executive Order 14289 and Proclamation 10925 provided that goods subject to the Section 232 automobile and parts duties do not also pay the IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico or the Section 232 steel and aluminum duties, and set up an import adjustment offset for parts used by U.S. vehicle assemblers.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025. Chinese bicycles, e-bikes and motorcycles paid it on top of the fentanyl and Section 301 duties until May 13, 2025; cars and auto parts were outside it.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on cars and light trucks (25%)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 (signed March 26, 2025) imposed 25% on passenger vehicles (sedans, SUVs, crossovers, minivans, cargo vans) and light trucks from every country for goods entered from April 3, 2025, new or used, and on top of FTA rates. USMCA vehicles may pay it only on their non-U.S. content once Commerce approves the U.S. content (9903.94.03; CSMS # 65649652).

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded, and goods subject to Section 232 duties — including the cars, light trucks and parts covered from April 3 and May 3, 2025 — left out. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Steel trailer wheel orders on China continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the 2019 antidumping and countervailing duty orders on steel trailer wheels 12 to 16.5 inches from China (8716.90.50.35, 8716.90.50.59).

changes.title: Russian aluminum duty raised to 200%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10895 kept the 200% duty on Russian aluminum and extended it to derivative articles (9903.85.68); in Chapter 87 it reaches aluminum derivative articles such as bumpers and trailers of Russian origin.

changes.title: USMCA goods exempted from the Canada and Mexico IEEPA duties
changes.detail: Executive Orders 14231 and 14232 exempted goods of Canada and Mexico that qualify for USMCA from the IEEPA duties from March 7, 2025 (9903.01.04, 9903.01.14). Ended with those duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the Section 301 lists. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on Mexican goods (9903.01.01), in force from March 4, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on Canadian goods (9903.01.10), in force from March 4, 2025, later raised to +35%. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Steel truck wheel orders on China continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the 2019 antidumping (231.70% China-wide) and countervailing (457.10%) duty orders on certain steel wheels of 22.5 and 24.5 inches from China (8708.70.45, 8708.70.60, 8716.90.50).

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on chassis from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued a countervailing duty order (44.32%, May 10, 2021) and an antidumping duty order (188.05% China-wide, July 8, 2021) on chassis and subassemblies from China, such as container chassis (8716.39.00.90, 8716.90.50).

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 87 goods were **$337.9B in 2025**, -13.7% from $391.5B in 2024. **Cars and other passenger vehicles** (8703) were $183.8B, **auto parts** (8708) $84.7B and **trucks** (8704) $41.7B; motorcycles, bicycles, trailers and the rest made up the balance.

**Mexico** ($124.2B, 37%) is the largest supplier of both vehicles and parts: $44.7B of cars, $34.2B of trucks and $35.2B of parts. **Japan** ($46.2B), **South Korea** ($38.3B) and **Germany** ($27.8B) ship mostly finished cars, while **Canada** ($45.8B) ships cars and parts within the North American production chain. **China** ($13.2B) ships mostly parts ($8.8B), with $1.8B of vehicles of 8703 (cars, golf carts and other small vehicles), $863M of trailers and smaller amounts of bicycles, e-bikes, wheelchairs and strollers; Chinese cars face 52.5%, and EVs 127.5%.

2025 is the latest full year of trade data, so it shows the first year of the Section 232 automobile duties (from April and May 2025) but not the truck duty (November 2025), the 2026 Section 301 duties or the Section 338 duty on Canada. UN Comtrade does not say which imports were claimed under USMCA, how much of each vehicle was U.S. content, or which listed articles were vehicle parts, which is what decides most of the Section 232 duty. Duty-collected figures aren’t available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Many Chapter 87 lines depend on what the article is used for, so a cell can show more than one total, labelled by the answer: **car or light-truck part** (Section 232 auto parts, note 33(g)), **truck or bus part** (Section 232 truck parts, note 38(i)), or **not a vehicle part** (neither: the base rate plus the Section 301 duty for the country).

For Mexico and Canada the **USMCA-qualifying** view applies the USMCA rules: Free base rates, no Section 232 duty on parts, and for cars, light trucks and heavy trucks 25% of the **non-U.S. content** (shown as 25%, the rate with no approved U.S. content; each dollar of U.S. content Commerce approves comes off the base the 25% is charged on). Buses pay 10% even under USMCA. UK cars are shown inside the 100,000-vehicle quota (10%); over the quota they pay 27.5%. AD/CVD deposits (chassis, van-type trailers, steel wheels, brake drums, golf carts, hand trucks) are not included.

rule.label: USMCA: cars, light trucks and heavy trucks 25% of the non-U.S. content (9903.94.03, 9903.74.03; U.S. content Commerce-approved, entered under 9903.94.02 / 9903.74.06 at 0%); USMCA car and truck parts Free (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10); buses +10% (9903.74.02); metals goods 25% (mobile equipment: 25% of the non-U.S. content and of U.S. content above 40%); other goods Free (9903.05.94). Without USMCA: base + 25% on vehicles and parts, + 10% Section 301 (9903.05.55) on other goods. The 25% IEEPA duty ended February 24, 2026.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.88.69 (Section 301).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Variant labels: "car or light-truck part" and "truck or bus part" price the listed article as a Section 232 auto or truck part; "not a vehicle part" prices it without those duties. Vehicles are priced as passenger vehicles, light trucks or medium- and heavy-duty vehicles; the reliefs for articles that are not (9903.94.02, 9903.74.05) and for vehicles 25 or more years old (9903.94.04, 9903.74.07) need the importer's confirmation and are not applied.
USMCA vehicles: the 25% of the non-U.S. content is shown with no approved U.S. content (so 25% of the full value); approved U.S. content lowers it. UK cars are shown inside the quota (10%).

Certified-parts elections (9903.94.07, 9903.94.33, 9903.94.45, 9903.94.55, 9903.94.65, 9903.94.69, 9903.74.09) are opt-in and not applied; the import adjustment offsets for U.S. assemblers are not modelled.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. Canadian motorcycles over 800 cc show as banned.

AD/CVD deposits are company-specific and not included: chassis (China, Mexico, Thailand, Vietnam), steel wheels and steel trailer wheels (China), brake drums (China, Türkiye), low-speed vehicles such as golf carts (China), hand trucks (China); van-type trailers (China, Mexico, Canada) are still under investigation with provisional deposits.
Admissibility is separate from duty: vehicles must meet EPA and NHTSA rules at entry (see Tariff engineering).
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2, 16, 20, 29, 30, 31, 33, 38, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. No Chapter 87 line is on the 2026 Section 301 general exemption lists (note 52(b)–(d)) or any country exception list (note 52(j)), or on the Brazil exemption list (note 50(a)(ii)); the vehicle, parts, truck, bus and metals headings are lifted from both duties by notes 52(f) and 50(a)(vi) (9903.05.90, 9903.05.07). Note 33(b) lists 17 subheadings of passenger vehicles and light trucks, note 33(g) 130 auto-parts provisions, note 33(j) the UK parts, note 38(b) the medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and note 38(i) their parts. Note 51(b)(3) lists 8703.10.50, 8703.21.01 and 8711.50.00 for Canada (8711.50 now banned under Proclamation 11063). China: notes 20 (Lists 1–4A) and 31(d) and 31(k); the note 20(vvv) exclusions for 8711.10.00.00, 8708.40.75.70 and 8716.40.00.00 run through November 9, 2026. Note 30(b) lists the Russia 35% lines.
